text:
Mattias Ekholm is 36 and still a fixture on Edmonton's blue line, playing almost 21 minutes a night. He has 3 goals and 11 points in 25 games, a quiet line for a defenseman who drives results the way he does.

The headline number is a luck one. The Oilers have scored 17.3 more goals than their chances deserve with Ekholm on the ice, the kind of figure that tends to shrink. That doesn't mean he's been bad: Edmonton wins 51.9% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five with him, and about eight points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him 98th percentile among defensemen last season for the chances his team created with him on, after accounting for teammates and competition.

What worries you is the team around him. Edmonton won six straight in mid-November, then lost four in a row to Tampa Bay, Carolina, St. Louis and Vegas, and Ekholm hasn't had a point in any of them. When the bounces even out, the Oilers will need the process he brings even more.
headline: Ekholm's on-ice luck has been enormous
